item.description:
New

  • OpenShelf in Shortcuts and Spotlight. Convert Files, Compress, Extract
    Text (OCR), Remove Background, Combine into PDF, Remove Audio, Read QR Codes
    and Add to Shelf are now actions in the Shortcuts app, so you can chain
    them, add them to a Finder Quick Action, or run them on everything that
    lands in a folder with a folder automation, no dragging needed. On macOS 26
    and later the main ones are in Spotlight too. They run entirely on your Mac,
    like the wheels, and save results next to the originals.
  • Signed and notarized by Apple. OpenShelf is now signed with a Developer
    ID and notarized, so it opens like any other downloaded app: no more
    "Apple could not verify" warning, Open Anyway or Terminal commands.
  • Install with Homebrew: brew install --cask manan-santoki/tap/openshelf,
    or brew tap manan-santoki/tap once and then brew install --cask openshelf.
    OpenShelf keeps updating itself as before.
  • About OpenShelf in the menu-bar menu shows the version, with links to
    openshelf.space and the source code.

Good to know

  • macOS asks for permissions once more. Because OpenShelf is now signed
    differently, macOS treats it as a new app for privacy permissions. The first
    time you use a feature that talks to Finder or to Pages, Numbers or Keynote,
    click OK when macOS asks again. Nothing else changes, and your settings
    and shelf are kept.
  • Updates now come from a dedicated feed. Nothing to do: this update switches
    over by itself.

Transcripts and subtitles, ODT and EPUB through Pandoc, and ebooks with
calibre, all from free tools you install yourself.

New

  • Transcripts and subtitles, made on your Mac. With
    whisper.cpp installed
    (brew install whisper-cpp) and a speech model in
    ~/Library/Application Support/OpenShelf/Models, the Convert wheel turns
    audio into TXT, SRT and VTT, and video into SRT and VTT. Nothing is
    uploaded. Without whisper.cpp or a model the wedges don't appear;
    Settings → Extra Formats says what's missing. OpenShelf never downloads
    whisper.cpp or its models itself.
  • ODT and EPUB through Pandoc. With Pandoc installed, Markdown, Word,
    HTML and RTF documents also convert to ODT, and EPUB books convert to
    Word, Markdown, HTML (pictures included), ODT and plain text, plus PDF
    when a typesetter such as Tectonic, Typst or MacTeX is installed. Without
    Pandoc an EPUB offers ZIP, TAR and TAR.GZ, as before.
  • Ebooks with calibre. With calibre
    installed (brew install --cask calibre), EPUB, MOBI and AZW3 books
    convert to each other and to PDF, and PDFs convert to MOBI and AZW3, with
    progress. OpenShelf never installs calibre; without it nothing changes.
